## Dial 1.0.12 — 25 Oct 2026

- **Studio — a camera and live-streaming room (⌥⌘S).** Everything a camera control app does, inside Dial: pick and name your cameras and microphones; set exposure, white balance, focus, zoom, colour, sharpness, anti-flicker, HDR, mirror and rotate (on the camera when it allows, else by Dial); automatic framing that follows you (close-up, upper body, group, desk) with presets you recall by hotkey, phone or OSC; beauty, filters, background blur or colour, green screen, text, lower thirds, a clock, an image, Dial's level meter and picture-in-picture; a teleprompter; horizontal or vertical (9:16) output. Record the finished picture, send it to OBS, and **go live on YouTube, Twitch, Facebook, Kick and your own servers at the same time** from one encode, with a health line for each and automatic reconnects (several at once is Pro). Stream keys stay in the macOS keychain. A phone on the same Wi-Fi becomes a remote by scanning a QR code. (A true virtual camera needs Apple's Developer ID, which Dial doesn't have yet — Send to OBS stands in for it.)
- **Much more on right-click.** The window, Mixer, menu bar and Dock menus gain Quick Actions (reset every app to 100 %, save these volumes as a profile, copy the mixer as text, export and import settings), "Mute the others, keep this" and "Send to headphones / speakers" for each app, Device Actions (use for input and output, sample rate, rename, forget, balance), a volume limit and "pause instead of muting" for the sleep timer, the window layout and sound pack lists, and Studio.
- **25 more Finder actions (79 in all).** For sound files: play backwards, pitch up or down, remove or isolate the vocals, 8D audio, more bass or treble, loop three times, a 15-second preview, 44.1 / 48 kHz, add silence, cut in half, a ringtone from the loudest 30 seconds, and join several files into one. For videos: a picture at 1 second, a 6-second GIF, twice the speed, tall 9:16, Dial's level meter on the picture, and subtitles burnt in from the .srt next to it. For folders: a playlist, the total playing time and a loudness report.
- **24 window layouts and 28 list layouts** (8 more of each: Deck, Mosaic, Rail right, Split, Zen, Terminal, Tabs bottom, Cards; Ledger, Bubbles, Wide rows, Mini rows, Cover, Three columns, Colour bands, Focus), each with a preview in Settings → Appearance.
- **Smaller windows than ever.** Every view fits down to 380 × 300 with nothing overlapping or scrolling sideways; toolbars fold into a ⋯ menu under 560 px and two-column panels stack under 480 px.
- **6 more sound packs (20 in all: Piano, Kalimba, Harp, Drum, Radio, Crystal), 38 more sounds with their own animations, 42 more drawings** (a picture for every view, empty lists, splash variants), and more colour: file names by kind, the apps and devices playing now, code, JSON and log lines with brackets coloured by depth, and tinted list columns — still never pink.
- **Boost up to 20000 % (Pro).** Every slider, menu, hotkey, link, profile, the Dock and the volume HUD go to 20000 %; a new look-ahead limiter keeps even ×200 clean and can never turn sound into silence or noise, and a second hearing warning comes past 5000 % ("this can damage hearing and speakers").
- **No more apps going silent under heavy use (macOS).** With many videos looping, pausing and restarting at once (live streams, YouTube loops, Cine), a sound path that went quiet twice used to stay quiet — the app was muted until it stopped playing. Now a path that can't be fixed within 2 seconds lets the app play on its own, unprocessed, and Dial tries again after 20 s, 1 min and 3 min; a rebuilt path is ready before the old one is removed, so there is no gap.
- **AirPods and other Bluetooth headphones as the speaker.** Choosing them in the menu bar or the window connects them if needed, waits for macOS to make them an output, then switches — and says in plain words when macOS refuses. A connected device that isn't playing yet shows a "Use" button.
- **Your Mac never runs flat on the charger because of Dial.** When Dial held the charge limit by switching wall power off, a restart (or a low limit with a wide range) could leave the power off and the battery drained to 0 % with the charger plugged in. Now the charger always comes back: at start, at quit, after a crash, when Dial's control stops for a minute, when a battery reading fails, under a 20 % floor, and through the background helper even when Dial isn't running. Under 10 % on the charger and not charging, Dial gives the battery its charger back and tells you. Battery → Control shows what Dial is doing right now, with a **Stop controlling** button. Calibration now stops at 15 %, and a discharge no longer carries on after a restart.
- **Brightness keys on any keyboard.** F1 / F2 (and F14 / F15 on Apple-layout keyboards) change the brightness of the external display under the pointer from external keyboards too, and from the Touch Bar — and they work without the Accessibility permission (macOS then also sees the key). Hold fn (or ⇧) to type F1 / F2 into an app. On a keyboard set to media keys, F10–F12 drive Dial's own volume shortcuts when you put them there.
- **New Pro prices:** ₹1,000 a month or ₹6,000 a year (half the monthly price). Earlier subscribers keep the price they signed up at.
- **Dial is a Mac app for Apple silicon.** New versions are built for Apple silicon Macs only; earlier Intel, Windows and Linux installers stay downloadable but are no longer updated.
- **Fewer permission prompts after updates.** macOS remembers what you allowed (folders, network, recording) by the app's signature; every release is now signed with the same certificate and checked against the previous one before it goes out, so updates keep your answers.
- **The Dial web page and shop no longer run out of their daily allowance.** Their data moved to Dial's own accounts service.
- **Safer by default.** The Studio camera feed for OBS answers only on this Mac (never on the Wi-Fi, never to a web page), and the phone remote's link can't be guessed. Exported settings never contain your AI service keys. A Pro code is never dropped because the server had a hiccup — only when it is still unknown a day later.
- **Faster start, lighter running.** The window comes first: the Dock and Finder hooks, the menu-bar icon, the hotkeys and the mini mixer follow right after it is on screen, so the work before the first picture is about a fifth of what it was (clicking the menu-bar icon early still opens the mini mixer). The Visualizer uses about a third of the CPU (glows without blur), the app tamer and the temperature checks share one timer and wake far less often, and the mini mixer, HUD and camera bubble load about a fifth less style.
- **About the same size with much more inside.** The menu-bar icons are now packed when Dial is built, so the app carries no picture decoder (−137 KB) — that pays for a good part of Studio and the rest of this release, and the Mac download stays about 3.8 MB. Reaching 3 MB would mean dropping the built-in updater and its secure downloads, so they stay.

### Install

Dial is a Mac app (Apple silicon — M1 and later). One download: `Dial_<version>_aarch64.dmg`.

- **With Pour:** `curl -fsSL https://ipconfig.co.network/pour/install | sh` then `pour install --cask dial`
- **By hand:** open the DMG and drag Dial into Applications. First launch: `xattr -cr /Applications/Dial.app` (Dial is self-signed, not notarized).
- Per-app volume and the equaliser need macOS 14.4 or later.
- Earlier Windows, Linux, ChromeOS, FreeBSD and Intel Mac builds stay on the releases page but are no longer updated.
